article.title: Why Percentages Need Their Denominators
article.why: Prevent misleading trend stories by keeping ratios tied to the populations behind them.

paragraphs.en:
Dashboards often show percentages because percentages are easy to compare. A retention rate of 72%, a campaign response rate of 1.4%, or a defect rate of 0.3% can quickly summarize performance. But a percentage can become misleading when the denominator changes in a way that is not visible.

Suppose a campaign response rate rises from 1.0% to 1.4%. That sounds like a strong improvement. Yet the first campaign may have been sent to one million eligible customers, while the second was sent only to a carefully filtered group of 300,000. The higher rate may reflect better targeting, but total conversions could still be lower.

The same issue appears in retention. If a company changes the definition of an active customer, the denominator can shrink. A stable number of retained customers divided by a smaller eligible base produces a higher retention rate even though customer behavior did not improve.

For every important ratio, analysts should therefore document the numerator and denominator explicitly. A dashboard can show not only ‘response rate 1.4%’ but also ‘4,200 conversions / 300,000 delivered messages.’ This simple addition makes scale visible.

Trend reviews should also check eligibility rules. Did consent requirements change? Were inactive accounts removed? Did a new data-quality filter exclude records? Did the observation window move? These operational changes can alter the denominator and create an artificial break in the time series.

Absolute counts and rates should usually be reviewed together. Rates help compare populations of different sizes, while counts show total business volume. Neither is sufficient alone. A falling rate with rapidly growing volume may still create more total value; a rising rate with a collapsing denominator may signal shrinking opportunity.

A useful habit is to ask, ‘What had to be true for a record to enter this denominator?’ That question often reveals hidden business logic that is more important than the percentage itself.

Percentages are not deceptive by nature. They become deceptive when the population behind them is treated as fixed even though it changed. Good reporting keeps the ratio and its population together, so decision makers can see both performance and scale.

This principle matters especially when teams compare periods. If the denominator definition changes in April, a year-over-year chart may mix a genuine behavior change with a measurement change. Annotating definition changes on the chart, or restating historical data under a common rule when possible, prevents false trend narratives.

Segment-level ratios need the same discipline. A channel may show a higher response rate simply because low-propensity customers were removed from eligibility. Comparing only rates can make one channel look superior even when it produces fewer incremental conversions or less contribution margin.

For recurring reporting, denominator governance should be treated like metric governance. The eligibility rule, exclusion logic, observation window, and deduplication rule should be versioned and documented. When any of them changes, the dashboard should make the break visible instead of silently connecting incomparable periods.

A useful review question is therefore not just ‘Did the rate improve?’ but ‘Did the population represented by the rate stay comparable?’ This small shift in wording often prevents teams from celebrating a metric movement that was created by filtering rather than by better customer behavior.

That comparison should be repeated whenever targeting, consent rules, delivery filters, or active-customer definitions change, because those operational choices directly reshape the population behind the percentage.
paragraphs.zh:
Dashboard 常用 percentage，因為百分比容易比較。Retention 72%、campaign response 1.4%、defect 0.3% 都能快速摘要表現；但若 denominator 在不顯眼的地方改變，percentage 就可能誤導。

假設 response rate 從1.0%升到1.4%，看起來改善很多。但第一次可能投放100萬 eligible customers，第二次只投放精篩後30萬人；rate 雖提高，total conversions 仍可能更少。

Retention 也一樣。若 active customer 定義改變、分母縮小，即使 retained customers 人數不變，較小 denominator 也會讓 retention rate 上升，並不代表行為真的改善。

因此重要 ratio 應同時明示 numerator 與 denominator。與其只寫 response rate 1.4%，不如同時顯示 4,200 conversions / 300,000 delivered messages，讓 scale 可見。

Trend review 還要檢查 eligibility rule：consent 是否改變？inactive account 是否移除？data-quality filter 是否新增？observation window 是否移動？這些都會改變 denominator，製造 artificial break。

Absolute counts 與 rates 通常應一起看。Rate 適合比較不同規模 population，count 顯示實際 business volume，兩者單獨都不夠。Rate 下滑但 volume 大增仍可能創造更多價值；rate 上升但 denominator 崩縮則可能代表 opportunity 變小。

一個好習慣是問：「一筆 record 要符合什麼條件才能進入這個 denominator？」這常會揭露比 percentage 本身更重要的 business logic。

Percentage 本身不會騙人，問題在於 population 已變卻被當成固定。好的 reporting 會把 ratio 與其 population 放在一起，讓決策者同時看到 performance 與 scale。

跨期比較時尤其如此。若4月改了 denominator definition，YoY chart 可能把真正 behavior change 與 measurement change 混在一起。最好在圖上標記定義改動，或能重算時用共同規則 restate historical data。

Segment-level ratio 也需要相同紀律。某 channel 的 response rate 可能只是因低 propensity customers 被排除而上升；只比 rates 會讓該 channel 看似優秀，即使 incremental conversions 或 contribution margin 更低。

Recurring reporting 中，denominator governance 應像 metric governance 一樣被管理。Eligibility、exclusion logic、observation window、deduplication rule 都應 versioned 並記錄，改動時 dashboard 要把 break 顯示出來。

因此 review 不只問「rate 有沒有改善」，還要問「這個 rate 代表的 population 是否仍可比較」。這能避免把 filtering 造成的變動誤當成顧客行為改善。

只要 targeting、consent、delivery filter 或 active-customer definition 改變，就應重新做這個檢查，因為這些 operational choices 會直接重塑 percentage 背後的 population。
paragraphs.ja:
dashboardではpercentageがよく使われます。retention 72%、campaign response 1.4%、defect 0.3%は比較しやすい一方、denominatorが見えないところで変わると誤解を生みます。

response rateが1.0%から1.4%へ上がっても、前年は100万人、今年は厳選した30万人への配信かもしれません。rateは高くてもtotal conversionは減っている可能性があります。

retentionも同じです。active customer定義を変えてdenominatorが縮小すれば、retained customer数が同じでもretention rateは上昇します。顧客行動が改善したとは限りません。

重要なratioではnumeratorとdenominatorを明示すべきです。「response rate 1.4%」だけでなく「4,200 conversions / 300,000 delivered messages」と表示すればscaleが見えます。

trend reviewではeligibility ruleも確認します。consent条件、inactive除外、data-quality filter、observation windowの変更はdenominatorを変え、time seriesにartificial breakを作ります。

absolute countとrateは通常セットで見ます。rateは異なるpopulation sizeを比較しやすく、countはbusiness volumeを示します。rateが下がってもvolume増で価値が増えることもあり、rateが上がってもdenominator急減ならopportunity縮小かもしれません。

「このdenominatorに入るために何がtrueである必要があるか」と問うと、percentageより重要なbusiness logicが見えることがあります。

percentageが問題なのではなく、背後のpopulationが変わっているのに固定とみなすことが問題です。ratioとpopulationを一緒に示せばperformanceとscaleを両方見られます。

period比較では特に重要です。4月にdenominator definitionが変わればyear-over-year chartはbehavior changeとmeasurement changeを混ぜます。chartにdefinition changeをannotateし、可能ならcommon ruleでhistoryをrestatementします。

segment ratioも同じです。low-propensity customerをeligibilityから外しただけでchannel responseが上がる場合があります。rateだけではincremental conversionやcontribution marginが少ないchannelを良く見せてしまいます。

denominator governanceはmetric governanceとして管理し、eligibility、exclusion logic、observation window、deduplication ruleをversioning・document化します。変更時はdashboard上でbreakを見せます。

reviewでは「rateが改善したか」だけでなく「そのrateが表すpopulationは比較可能か」を確認します。targeting、consent、delivery filter、active-customer definitionが変わるたびに同じ確認が必要です。

business.term: The rate improved, but the eligible population changed.
business.explanation: 避免把比例上升直接解讀為表現改善。
